evidence: Receiving DO2 50.0h: 11.63 mg/L then 50.2h: 6.47 mg/L, 50.4–52.0h stable ~6.2–7.0
Source batches DO2 at 52h: 10.88 (s1), 10.81 (s2), 11.47 (s3) mg/L — receiving diverges by ~4.4 mg/L
Receiving P at 48h: 3.24 g/L vs source 2.98–3.06 g/L — production on/ahead of schedule
Minimum DO2 constraint 2.0 mg/L currently satisfied with margin
Air increase bounded at 1.15; feed kept at 1.0 to retain product mass
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows a sharp, sustained step drop from ~11.6 to ~6.5 mg/L at 50.2 h that does not occur in any of the three source batches at the same process age (all ~10.8–11.5 mg/L), indicating a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit. DO2 is still above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, and product (3.24 g/L at 48 h) is slightly ahead of source batches, so production is healthy and should not be throttled. A bounded 15% increase in air (1.0 feed, 1.15 air) directly addresses the deficit while retaining full feed and product mass; stronger feed cuts would sacrifice growth for an oxygen margin that is not yet threatened.
args.uncertainty: The cause of the DO2 step-down is unknown (equipment fault, gas-transfer change, or metabolic demand shift); if it is a sensor artifact, extra air is harmless, but if DO2 continues falling despite +15% air, a feed reduction may be needed later. DO2 may also recover on its own, making the intervention merely margin-restoring rather than necessary. Only ~1.8 h of post-drop data is available.
